defaultPrescription: 2 sets of 10–15 repetitions, light–moderate effort, with 1–2 minutes between sets. Exhale through the effort. Confirm the expanded four-day split with your exercise clinician.
referenceNotes: Original exercise prescription, Sept 29 2026 (Group A, Group B and aerobic sessions). Public illustrations are original simplified movement diagrams—not copies of clinician handout photos. Adaptations are explicitly marked.

days.label: Day A
days.title: Lower body + core
days.intro: Squat and hip-hinge practice, hip stability and trunk control. Several movements come directly from clinician Group A.

cardio.prescription: Original session 1: elliptical 10–20 min + treadmill 10–20 min, accumulating at least 30 min light-to-moderate aerobic activity.

days.label: Day B
days.title: Upper body
days.intro: A full upper-body day combining prescribed Group A and B exercises; cable and dumbbell versions suit the photographed gym.

cardio.prescription: Original session 2: treadmill 30 minutes — 5-min warm-up, 5-min usual pace at 0%, 5-min at 3–5% incline, 5-min flat, 5-min incline, 5-min cooldown.

days.label: Day C
days.title: Lower body + glutes
days.intro: Alternatives to the leg-press, leg-extension and leg-curl machines in Group B, plus posterior-chain and core work. Review substitutions with your clinician.

cardio.prescription: Original session 3: elliptical 10–20 min + treadmill 10–20 min, accumulating at least 30 min light-to-moderate aerobic activity.

days.label: Day D
days.title: Upper body + core
days.intro: A second upper-body stimulus emphasizing pressing, back, shoulder stability and controlled core work.

cardio.prescription: Original session 4: bike 15–30 minutes; 3–5 min warm-up, 3–5 min usual pace, 3–5 min slightly higher resistance/speed, usual pace, higher resistance/speed, 3–5 min cooldown.

exercises.name: Goblet / bodyweight squat
exercises.origin: Group A — squat (dumbbell load is an option)
steps: Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart and brace gently.
Send hips back and bend knees; keep knees in line with toes.
Lower only as far as you can keep your back neutral.
Push through your feet to stand; breathe out on the rise.
exercises.avoid: Keep heels grounded. Use bodyweight or a box if depth/control is limited.

exercises.name: Unweighted good morning
exercises.equipment: Bodyweight; optional very light dumbbell only with approval
steps: Stand tall, soften knees and fold arms over your chest.
Push hips backward while tipping your torso forward.
Stop as soon as your back wants to round.
Drive hips forward to stand upright, breathing out.
exercises.avoid: Begin unweighted as shown in the clinician sheet; do not hinge through your lower back.

exercises.name: Standing hip abduction
steps: Hold a stable support, stand tall and keep hips facing forward.
Slowly lift one straight leg sideways with toes forward.
Pause briefly without leaning your trunk.
Lower with control; complete both sides.
exercises.avoid: Cable resistance requires an ankle strap not confirmed in the photos; bodyweight is the prescribed baseline.

exercises.name: Standing hip adduction
steps: Stand upright beside stable support, feet under hips.
Lift one leg slightly and move it across the body.
Keep the toes pointing forward and pelvis level.
Return slowly and change legs.
exercises.avoid: Do not swing or rotate the pelvis to move farther.

exercises.name: Low step-up
exercises.equipment: Low secure step or stair (not a high weight bench)
steps: Choose a low, nonslip, stable platform and stand close.
Place your full working foot on the step.
Press through that foot and stand tall without pushing hard off the trailing leg.
Step down slowly, then repeat; switch legs.
exercises.avoid: The photographed workout bench may be too high. Use a lower secure step; ask for an alternative if none is available.

exercises.name: Dead bug — leg extension
exercises.origin: Group A — dead bug: hip extension
steps: Lie on your back, arms up and hips/knees bent around 90 degrees.
Brace gently to keep lower back near the floor.
Slowly extend one leg away without arching the back.
Bring it back and alternate sides; exhale on extension.
exercises.avoid: Make the leg movement smaller if your back lifts or discomfort starts.

exercises.name: Standing calf raise
steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hold support if needed.
Rise smoothly onto the balls of both feet.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower heels slowly without bouncing.
exercises.avoid: Keep pressure even across the forefoot.

exercises.name: One-arm high cable pulldown
exercises.equipment: Functional trainer · high pulley · single handle
steps: Set a handle at the high cable and take a stable split stance.
Reach overhead with one arm and gently brace the torso.
Pull elbow down toward the ribs without twisting or arching.
Return the handle slowly overhead; repeat other arm.
exercises.avoid: Use a cable height/attachment that feels secure. This is a substitute for a lat-pulldown machine, not the same machine.

exercises.name: Flat dumbbell chest press
exercises.origin: Group B — chest press machine (dumbbell substitute)
steps: Lie on the bench, feet flat, dumbbells held by chest.
Gently draw shoulder blades back into the bench.
Press weights upward in a controlled line, exhaling.
Lower elbows slowly to a comfortable range.
exercises.avoid: Choose loads you can get into position safely. Avoid barbell bench pressing alone.

exercises.name: Standing / seated cable row
exercises.origin: Group B — seated close-grip row (cable variation)
exercises.equipment: Functional trainer · low cable · row handle
steps: Set cable low and position yourself facing it with stable feet.
Start with arms comfortably extended and spine tall.
Pull elbows back toward ribs, bringing handle toward the torso.
Squeeze shoulder blades gently, then return without leaning backward.
exercises.avoid: If a stable seated position isn't possible on this machine, stand with feet staggered.

exercises.name: Seated dumbbell shoulder press
exercises.origin: Group A — shoulder press machine (dumbbell alternative listed)
steps: Set bench upright and sit with feet planted.
Bring light dumbbells beside shoulders, wrists stacked over elbows.
Press toward the ceiling without arching your lower back.
Lower slowly, breathing in on the way down.
exercises.avoid: Do not force overhead movement through shoulder pain; check technique with your clinician.

exercises.name: Dumbbell lateral raise
steps: Stand tall holding light weights at your sides.
Soften elbows and raise arms out to the sides.
Stop near shoulder height or earlier if uncomfortable.
Lower slowly without shrugging.
exercises.avoid: Light weights and clean control matter more than lifting high.

exercises.name: Shoulder external rotation
exercises.equipment: No weight to start; optional very light cable if approved
steps: Stand or sit tall; bend elbows 90 degrees and tuck them at your sides.
Keeping elbows fixed, rotate forearms gently outward.
Pause within comfortable range.
Rotate back slowly without flaring elbows.
exercises.avoid: Unloaded is the starting form shown in the therapist handout.

exercises.name: Dumbbell biceps curl
steps: Stand or sit tall with dumbbells at sides, palms forward.
Keep elbows close and curl weights toward shoulders.
Avoid swinging torso or shoulders.
Slowly lower until elbows are comfortably straight.
exercises.avoid: Keep wrists neutral rather than bent back.

exercises.name: Cable triceps pushdown
exercises.origin: Group B — bilateral triceps extension pulley
steps: Stand tall facing high pulley, elbows close to ribs.
Begin with forearms bent and handle near lower chest.
Extend elbows to press handle toward hips, breathing out.
Slowly return without letting upper arms swing forward.
exercises.avoid: Use the attachment you actually have; avoid locking elbows aggressively.

exercises.name: Supported box squat
steps: Stand in front of a stable box/chair slightly wider than hip width.
Bend at hips and knees to lightly touch the seat.
Keep knees aligned over toes and torso controlled.
Stand through your feet without bouncing off the seat.
exercises.avoid: This is not an exact mechanical equivalent to a leg-press machine. Confirm with your clinician.

exercises.name: Seated knee extension (unloaded)
exercises.origin: Group B — knee extension machine (unloaded substitute)
steps: Sit upright on a stable seat with both feet touching floor.
Straighten one knee as far as is comfortable without snapping it.
Hold briefly while keeping the thigh supported.
Lower slowly; repeat the other leg.
exercises.avoid: This preserves the movement pattern, but not the machine's resistance. Ask whether a band option is suitable.

exercises.name: Standing knee flexion (unloaded)
exercises.origin: Group B — knee flexion machine (unloaded substitute)
exercises.equipment: Stable support; optional ankle cable only if equipped/approved
steps: Hold stable support and stand upright.
Bend one knee, bringing heel slowly toward your glutes.
Keep thighs near each other and pelvis still.
Lower foot slowly and switch sides.
exercises.avoid: This keeps knee-flexion movement but is lighter than a machine curl. Ask your clinician if added resistance is appropriate.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
exercises.origin: General resistance handout — added hip hinge
steps: Hold light dumbbells at thighs; soften knees.
Send hips straight backward, moving dumbbells close to legs.
Stop where back remains neutral, regardless of depth.
Stand by squeezing glutes, breathing out as you rise.
exercises.avoid: Not part of the specific A/B prescription; use only if your clinician approves the extra hinge work.

exercises.name: Glute bridge
exercises.equipment: Mat / floor; optional light dumbbell later
steps: Lie on back, knees bent, feet flat and arms beside body.
Brace gently and press through heels to lift hips.
Stop when shoulders, hips and knees form a comfortable line.
Pause then lower vertebra by vertebra, without over-arching.
exercises.avoid: Start bodyweight as in the supplied clinician sheet.

exercises.name: Four-point leg raise
exercises.origin: Group A — four points plus leg raise
steps: Start on hands and knees, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Brace gently and reach one leg straight back.
Keep hips level and avoid arching the lower back.
Lower the knee and alternate sides.
exercises.avoid: Use the leg-only version first; adding opposite-arm reach is a progression.

exercises.name: Incline dumbbell chest press
steps: Set bench to a low incline, sit and settle dumbbells beside chest.
Plant feet and keep head/back supported.
Press weights up, exhaling, without bumping them together.
Lower slowly until elbows remain in a comfortable range.
exercises.avoid: Use light dumbbells and a modest incline to avoid excess shoulder load.

exercises.name: One-arm cable row
steps: Face the cable and stagger your feet for stability.
Reach forward with one hand, keeping ribs over hips.
Pull elbow back toward your hip, without torso rotation.
Slowly return and switch arms.
exercises.avoid: Keep weight light enough to avoid twisting.

exercises.name: Cable face pull
exercises.origin: General resistance principles — optional shoulder accessory
exercises.equipment: Functional trainer · high cable · rope/paired handles
steps: Set cable around face height and hold rope/handles.
Stand tall and pull handles toward either side of your face.
Allow elbows to flare outward comfortably as shoulder blades draw back.
Return slowly without leaning or arching.
exercises.avoid: Skip if the necessary attachment is unavailable or it irritates your shoulders.

exercises.name: Dumbbell hammer curl
steps: Hold dumbbells at sides with palms facing thighs.
Keep elbows near the body as you curl upward.
Pause without rocking the torso.
Lower slowly to start.
exercises.avoid: Keep forearms neutral throughout.

exercises.name: Overhead hold + marching
exercises.origin: Group B — marching in place holding one weight overhead
exercises.equipment: Very light dumbbell or unweighted first
steps: Stand tall holding one light weight overhead only if approved and steady.
Brace trunk without holding your breath.
Raise one knee slowly and lower it.
Alternate knees; switch holding arms between sets if comfortable.
exercises.avoid: Balance first: march with arms down if overhead loading is uncomfortable or unsteady.
